summary: An interactive 3D satellite story map built in Google Earth that solves a major Earth science paradox: how identical global climate forcing drives contrasting regional temperature trends. Using NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis data (2016–2024) with seasonal cycles removed and 95% confidence intervals validated via the KNMI Climate Explorer, this no-code educational tool compares four distinct biomes—Abu Dhabi, Al Khatim Desert, the Amazon Rainforest, and the Arctic—to make climate statistics accessible and inspire local urban cooling solutions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Earth System Trend Detective is a no-code, interactive 3D satellite story map built in Google Earth that explains how identical global climate forcing drives contrasting regional temperature trends. Using NASA MERRA-2 2-meter air temperature reanalysis data (2016–2024) processed through the KNMI Climate Explorer, the project removes regular seasonal cycles and plots 95% confidence bounds across four distinct biomes:

  • Abu Dhabi Coastal & Urban Belt (24.0°–24.8°N, 54.0°–54.8°E): Anomalies shifted from -1.5°C (2016–2019) to sustained spikes of +1.0°C to +1.5°C (2021–2024), exceeding the 97.5% upper confidence bound due to urban concrete and coastal humidity.
  • Al Khatim Inland Desert (23.5°–24.2°N, 54.8°–55.6°E): Lacking coastal moisture or asphalt, anomalies stay tightly contained within a narrow -0.5°C to +0.5°C band with faster nighttime cooling.
  • Manaus, Central Amazon Basin (2.0°–4.0°S, 60.0°–62.0°W): Dense forest canopy evapotranspiration acts as a natural cooling buffer, keeping anomalies centered near 0°C.
  • Longyearbyen, Svalbard Arctic (77.5°–79.0°N, 14.0°–18.0°E): Melting snow and sea ice expose dark ocean water, driving extreme polar amplification swings from -6°C to +4°C.

Impact, Tools & Creativity
Developed solo (Solo System Architect, Abu Dhabi Hub) using NASA MERRA-2, KNMI Climate Explorer, and Google Earth, this project turns complex climate statistics into an accessible visual story. Contrasting Abu Dhabi's urban heat trend against natural moisture buffers also highlights practical local solutions: expanding green corridors, reflective cool roofs, and coastal mangrove restoration.
